desc:
The string s consists of '(', ')' and '?'. Every '?' has to be replaced by a bracket. Let q be the number of question marks. The arrays a and b both have length q: the k-th question mark (from the left, 0-based) costs a[k] if you replace it by '(' and b[k] if you replace it by ')'.

The final string must be well-formed: every '(' is closed by a later ')', every ')' closes an earlier '(', and nothing is left open. Return the minimum total cost of the replacements, or -1 if no choice gives a well-formed string.

For example, s = "??", a = [5, 1], b = [1, 5] has only one valid result, "()", and costs a[0] + b[1] = 10.
constraints: a.length = b.length = number of ? in s
hints: Try the cheap-looking assumption first: turn every '?' into ')' and pay b[k] for each. What goes wrong while scanning from the left?

The balance becomes negative at some point. You must have chosen '(' for at least one earlier question mark. Changing one question mark from ')' to '(' adds 2 to every later balance and changes the cost by a[k] - b[k].

Scan left to right, push a[k] - b[k] of every question mark you pass into a min-heap, and whenever the balance drops below 0 pop the smallest value, add it to the cost and raise the balance by 2 (if the heap is empty the answer is -1). At the end the balance must be exactly 0.
editorial: Start with the assumption that all question marks are ')' and pay the sum of b[k]. While scanning, keep the balance. The first moment the balance is negative, some earlier question mark must become '('; flipping the candidate with the smallest extra cost a[k] - b[k] is the cheapest repair and raises every later prefix balance by 2. The heap holds the candidates seen so far (flipped ones are removed, so each is used once).

The greedy choice is safe because a flip at any earlier position fixes the current violation equally well and also helps all later positions, so the cheapest available flip can always be exchanged into an optimal solution. Flips are only done when forced, so their number is minimal. If the heap is empty when the balance is negative, or the balance at the end is not 0 (the sequence has too many opening brackets, or an odd length), no completion exists. Time O(n log n), space O(n).
